questions.q: Which part is AI, and which part is ordinary C#?
questions.answer: Gemma proposes likelihood and impact from the supplied evidence. C# validates the reply, multiplies the ratings, orders the risks, and displays the brief.
questions.technical: AiRiskService sends one local request. RiskEstimate stores proposed values separately from Risk. CalculateScore returns likelihood times impact; FormatBrief orders those calculated values.

questions.q: Does a score of 20 out of 25 mean an 80% chance of failure?
questions.answer: No. It is a priority ranking made by multiplying two ordinal ratings.
questions.technical: The project has no trained probability model, calibration data, or validation of real-world failure rates. Model ratings are judgments for review.

questions.q: Is this connected to a real email account?
questions.answer: No. It reads fictional .eml, .txt, and .json files from DemoData each time a brief is requested.
questions.technical: LoadEvidence reads explicitly listed local files and assigns source IDs from their filenames. No mail API or message-sending code is used.

questions.q: Why does closing one Inventory risk not make it OnTrack?
questions.answer: Other risks are still open. Closing INV-1 leaves INV-2 and INV-3, which keep Inventory AtRisk.
questions.technical: CalculateHealth scans the whole risk list. Any open risk with stored impact at least 4 takes precedence; otherwise any open risk gives AtRisk.

questions.q: Why have both Risk and RiskEstimate?
questions.answer: Risk stores the project's original record; RiskEstimate holds separate model advice.
questions.technical: The service does not assign model ratings back into Risk. It validates and sorts the estimate list, so stored health and ratings are unchanged by inference.

questions.q: What does a valid citation prove?
questions.answer: It proves the model named a permitted source for that risk. A person must still check whether the explanation is supported by the source.
questions.technical: ValidateEstimates checks that source IDs exist in the evidence dictionary and are assigned to the matching risk. It does not independently verify every sentence.

questions.q: Why can selectedProject change the project in the list?
questions.answer: It refers to the same Project object, not a new copy.
questions.technical: Project is a reference type. SelectProject returns a reference to an existing object. ChangeStatus mutates that object after validating the supplied choice.

questions.q: What happens when there are no open risks or Bionic is unavailable?
questions.answer: An empty risk list can still receive a brief about health and milestones. If the local request fails, the app displays an error and returns to the menu.
questions.technical: The model must return no risk estimates when there are no open risks. Timeouts, connection problems, and invalid reply data are handled without inventing an assessment.
